# Sirach Chapter 43 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalent)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 43 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**43:1** The vault of heaven, crystalline and clear, is the crown of the heights. The sky's appearance — it is a vision of glory.

**43:2** The sun, rising into view, announces itself: what a marvel it is! What a work of the Most High!

**43:3** At noon it dries out the land. Who can stand up to its scorching heat?

**43:4** A furnace-stoker swelters in the heat, but the sun scorches the mountains three times over. It breathes out blazing vapor, shoots out blinding rays, dazzles the eyes with its light.

**43:5** Great is the Lord who made it! At his word it races on its course.

**43:6** The moon, too, marks the times in all its phases — a sign of seasons and a signal for the world.

**43:7** From the moon comes the reckoning of feast days; a light that fades once it reaches its full.

**43:8** The month takes its name from the moon, marvelously growing as it changes, guiding the armies of heaven on high, brilliant in the firmament of the sky.

**43:9** The splendor of the stars — glory of the skies! A glittering ornament in the heights where the Lord dwells.

**43:10** At the word of the Holy One they stand in formation; they never nod off at their watch.

**43:11** Look at the rainbow and bless its Maker! It blazes with extraordinary beauty.

**43:12** It curves in its radiant arc across the sky, drawn by the hands of the Most High.

**43:13** At his command he drives the snow; he hurls down flashes of his judgment.

**43:14** The storehouses of heaven open, and the clouds stream out like birds in flight.

**43:15** In his might he makes the clouds dense; the hailstones are shattered to fragments.

**43:16** The sound of his thunder shakes the earth; the northern storm breaks loose, and the whirlwind.

**43:17** He scatters snow like birds alighting; it settles like locusts descending.

**43:18** The eye marvels at the whiteness of it; the heart stands in awe as it falls.

**43:19** He pours frost over the earth like a scattering of salt; when it freezes, it becomes needlepoints of ice.

**43:20** The cold north wind blows and ice seizes the water; it forms over every pond; the water is clad as if in armor.

**43:21** It eats up the mountains, scorches the wilderness, withers the green grass like fire.

**43:22** Then a mist rolls in and heals everything; dew falls after the heat and brings relief.

**43:23** By his wisdom he calmed the great deep and planted islands in it.

**43:24** Those who sail the sea tell of its terrors; we hear them and are struck with awe.

**43:25** There he has his most astonishing works: strange and wonderful creatures of every kind, all manner of living things, and the great sea monsters.

**43:26** Because of him his messenger accomplishes its task; and at his word all things hold together.

**43:27** We could go on speaking, and never say enough. Let this be the final word: He is the all.

**43:28** Where do we find the strength to praise him? He is greater than all his works.

**43:29** The Lord is awesome, utterly great; his power is astounding.

**43:30** Praise the Lord and lift him as high as you can — he still surpasses you. Summon all your strength to exalt him; do not grow tired, for you will never reach the end.

**43:31** Who has ever seen him and can describe him? Who can praise him as he deserves?

**43:32** Many things greater than these remain hidden; we have glimpsed only a handful of his works.

**43:33** For the Lord made all things, and to those who are faithful he has given wisdom.
